prompt: Write 5 short claim log entries by an auto insurance adjuster for a rear-end collision claim. Injury: neck and back strain. The claimant is not represented by a lawyer. Start each entry on a new line with 'Entry 1:', 'Entry 2:' and so on. No names, dates or amounts. (Internal reference C-1166; do not mention it.)
text:
Entry 1: Claim opened following a rear-end collision at a signalized intersection. Insured vehicle was stopped at the light when struck from behind by a third-party vehicle. Claimant reports neck and back pain at the scene and was transported to urgent care. Police report requested. Liability appears clear based on the initial statements.

Entry 2: Spoke with claimant by phone. Claimant is not represented by an attorney and says they are handling the matter directly. Claimant describes stiffness in the neck, lower back pain, and difficulty sleeping. Advised claimant of the medical payments coverage available under the policy and provided the claim number for future reference.

Entry 3: Received urgent care records. Diagnosis listed as cervical and lumbar strain with prescribed muscle relaxers and a referral to a physical therapist. No fractures or imaging findings noted. Claimant has scheduled initial physical therapy sessions. Reserve adjusted to reflect expected medical treatment duration.

Entry 4: Obtained photographs of both vehicles from the claimant and the insured. Damage to the rear of the claimant's vehicle is consistent with the reported impact. Third-party vehicle damage is confined to the front bumper area. Repair estimates requested from the preferred body shop network.

Entry 5: Follow-up call with claimant to check on treatment progress. Claimant reports partial improvement in neck mobility but ongoing back discomfort when sitting for long periods. Reminded claimant to keep all treatment appointments and to forward any new medical bills as they arrive. File remains open pending physical therapy progress notes.
